rich_summary: Kadru and Vinata discover the celestial horse whose white body has black hairs in its tail, proving Kadru’s claim and forcing the sorrowful Vinata into slavery after losing their wager. Soon after, Vinata’s son Garuda bursts from his egg in overwhelming radiance, blazing like cosmic fire and expanding to colossal size as he ascends the sky. The gods, terrified by the brilliance, mistake him for a consuming flame until Agni explains that this being is Garuda, son of Kasyapa and destined foe of the Nagas. The gods praise him with a vast hymn, and Garuda mercifully reduces his blazing form. He then departs, carrying his brother Aruna and placing him in the eastern sky just as the sun prepares to rise.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the wager’s outcome that condemns Vinata to slavery, setting the central motivation for Garuda’s later actions.
Describes the dramatic birth of Garuda, whose emergence without his mother and blazing power mark him as a cosmic being.
The gods mistake Garuda’s radiance for destructive fire, emphasizing the overwhelming scale of his power.
Part of the grand hymn in which the gods identify Garuda with multiple cosmic principles, revealing his mythic and theological significance.
Garuda calms the frightened gods and continues his cosmic role, carrying Aruna to the eastern sky to herald the rising sun.

top_scenes.scene_text: Garuda bursts from the egg in a blaze of golden fire, wings expanding as lightning-bright eyes illuminate the heavens.
The gods scatter across the sky in their celestial chariots, shielding their eyes from Garuda’s blazing radiance like a second sun.
Garuda soars over the ocean carrying Aruna on his back and sets him in the eastern sky as the sun prepares to rise.
